weeks.title: Claim the Throne
weeks.question: Whose life am I actually building?

days.title: The borrowed life
days.action: Record the baseline scenario before teaching. Audit yesterday’s time, attention and promises.
days.evidence: Baseline response plus three approval-driven choices.
days.retrieval: What did I choose, and what did I assume I had to do?

days.title: Your interests count
days.action: Write a one-page doctrine: what matters, what it costs, responsibilities and one protected priority.
days.evidence: Doctrine v1 with a specific resource allocation.
days.retrieval: Explain self-interest without confusing it with impulse.

days.title: The first no
days.action: Rehearse a proportionate refusal, then use it on an appropriate low-stakes request.
days.evidence: Boundary record: words, predicted reaction, actual reaction and reflection.
days.retrieval: Recall yesterday’s protected priority without notes.

days.title: Release the label
days.action: Choose a limiting identity claim and take one small action that tests it.
days.evidence: Old label, test action and observed result.
days.retrieval: Recall the first no and what the response actually showed.

days.title: Choose the Doom Project
days.action: Choose audience, useful deliverable, available time and a six-week success criterion. Take the first step.
days.evidence: One-page project charter plus first action.
days.retrieval: Which automatic yes could threaten this mission?

days.title: Council: claim your mission
days.action: Present the doctrine and project; practise responding to one reasonable objection.
days.evidence: Feedback, one revision and next commitment.
days.retrieval: Explain the difference between disapproval and useful criticism.

days.title: The first reckoning
days.action: Review week-one evidence. Choose what to stop, keep and protect next week.
days.evidence: Weekly review and next week’s protected sessions.
days.retrieval: Recall the doctrine and one example of choosing freely.

weeks.title: Build the Fortress
weeks.question: Can I trust myself to execute?

days.title: Price the yes
days.action: Use M01 to examine three commitments and renegotiate one appropriate demand.
days.evidence: Opportunity-cost ledger and calendar adjustment.
days.retrieval: Recall the doctrine and first boundary.

days.title: Control the gates
days.action: Use M02 to separate control, influence and external conditions. Build an interruption plan.
days.evidence: Control map plus one if–then plan.
days.retrieval: Explain M01 using a real choice.

days.title: Forge readiness
days.action: Select an appropriate movement/recovery practice and protect one focused session.
days.evidence: Readiness baseline and realistic daily command sheet.
days.retrieval: Which week-one boundary makes this possible?

days.title: Keep a small promise
days.action: Complete a defined project task during protected time; respond deliberately to interruption.
days.evidence: Work output and daily command record.
days.retrieval: Recall M01 and M02 without notes.

days.title: Repair and resume
days.action: Debrief a real disruption; if none occurred, rehearse losing a planned session.
days.evidence: Constraint, controllable response and feasible restart plan.
days.retrieval: Distinguish accountability from total control.

days.title: Council: stress the system
days.action: Explain the operating system; receive a scheduling disruption and revise it.
days.evidence: Revised command sheet with a defended trade-off.
days.retrieval: Revisit the first no under a stronger competing demand.

days.title: Maintain the fortress
days.action: Review promises and actual output. Remove one source of friction.
days.evidence: Weekly review with one system correction.
days.retrieval: Retrieve both models and one useful application each.

days.title: Reduce to requirements
days.action: Use M03 on the Doom Project. Mark each assumption and test the most important one.
days.evidence: Requirements sheet with a checked assumption.
days.retrieval: Reapply M01: what can be omitted?

days.title: Design against failure
days.action: Use M04 to identify likely failure routes and one preventive action each.
days.evidence: Three-risk prevention sheet.
days.retrieval: Recall M02 and separate prevention from external uncertainty.

days.title: Practise a useful subskill
days.action: Choose a task, baseline standard and feedback source. Run two short practice attempts.
days.evidence: Before/after output with specific feedback.
days.retrieval: Recall a limiting label and how evidence challenges it.

days.title: Build the first version
days.action: Produce a minimal working project output during protected time.
days.evidence: Prototype v1 that another person can inspect.
days.retrieval: Use a boundary to stop a distraction or added scope.

days.title: Build the Doombot
days.action: Test a reusable aid on one bounded task; compare with a manual result.
days.evidence: Aid, test case, quality check and keep/change/discard decision.
days.retrieval: Retrieve M03 and M04 and select the one needed now.

days.title: Council: show the work
days.action: Demonstrate the skill and prototype. Explain one failed assumption and correction.
days.evidence: Demonstration feedback and revision priority.
days.retrieval: Revisit self-belief as action plus correction.

days.title: Consolidate capability
days.action: Review improvement and select the next practice target.
days.evidence: Skill record and next-week project plan.
days.retrieval: Choose two older models and explain when each would mislead.

weeks.title: Command the Room
weeks.question: Can I pursue my interests in contact with other people?

days.title: Map the interests
days.action: Use M05 to prepare a real conversation. Identify unanswered questions about the other party.
days.evidence: Interest map separating evidence and inference.
days.retrieval: Recall the first no and apply it to a stronger demand.

days.title: Think beyond the answer
days.action: Use M06 to compare accepting, negotiating and declining a proposal.
days.evidence: Consequences sheet including a future cost.
days.retrieval: Reuse opportunity cost rather than inventing a new framework.

days.title: Make the request
days.action: Write a concise pitch and rehearse a specific ask with alternatives.
days.evidence: Recorded or written rehearsal and feedback.
days.retrieval: Explain which assumption needs checking.

days.title: Hold a real conversation
days.action: Conduct an appropriate pitch, boundary conversation or negotiation.
days.evidence: Privacy-conscious factual account of what was said and agreed.
days.retrieval: Select an earlier model without a facilitator prompt.

days.title: Debrief the response
days.action: Separate rejection, actionable criticism and uncertainty. Decide whether to persist, change or withdraw.
days.evidence: Debrief and a proportionate follow-up action.
days.retrieval: Revisit self-belief without ignoring valid criticism.

days.title: Council: hold your frame
days.action: Role-play a reasonable challenge with agreed limits. Explain your decision.
days.evidence: Feedback and improved response.
days.retrieval: Combine a boundary, M05 and M06.

days.title: Choose your next engagement
days.action: Review conversations, promises and project progress.
days.evidence: Next engagement plan with continue/change/withdraw criteria.
days.retrieval: Recall all six available models and select one relevant pair.

weeks.title: Build the Empire
weeks.question: Can I turn capability into useful value?

days.title: Locate the value
days.action: Use M07 to choose the work that most improves the audience’s result.
days.evidence: Audience/problem statement and one leverage hypothesis.
days.retrieval: Recall protected interests and the scope boundary.

days.title: Choose a useful signal
days.action: Use M08 to set a measure, feedback route and revision threshold.
days.evidence: Feedback plan with review date and limits.
days.retrieval: Use incentives to consider whether polite praise is reliable evidence.

days.title: Construct the offer
days.action: Prepare a clear release, service pilot or participation invitation.
days.evidence: Offer sheet with scope, costs and explicit ask.
days.retrieval: Reuse second-order consequences to check commitments.

days.title: Put it into the world
days.action: Expose the project to intended users and ask for a meaningful commitment.
days.evidence: Offer/release evidence and actual responses, including no response.
days.retrieval: Select prior models and justify their use.

days.title: Revise from reality
days.action: Review what users actually did. Improve the offer or delivery and test again where feasible.
days.evidence: Version comparison and a justified revision.
days.retrieval: Distinguish persistence from repeating an untested assumption.

days.title: Council: defend the value
days.action: Demonstrate the offer and evidence. Explain what remains uncertain.
days.evidence: Peer review and one delivery-system correction.
days.retrieval: Combine self-interest, negotiation and feedback.

days.title: Prepare for Doomsday
days.action: Identify remaining gaps, dependencies and a manageable final deliverable.
days.evidence: Completion plan and evidence inventory.
days.retrieval: Recall an older boundary and explain how it protects delivery.

weeks.title: Become Dangerous
weeks.question: Can I retain judgement when circumstances change?

days.title: Name the uncertainty
days.action: Use M09 to map remaining unknowns and choose one useful check.
days.evidence: Confidence statement, evidence and update condition.
days.retrieval: Recall M03/M04 and identify a surviving assumption.

days.title: Build the margin
days.action: Use M10 to prepare a realistic contingency and buffer.
days.evidence: Contingency sheet with explicit limits and trade-offs.
days.retrieval: Reuse opportunity cost: buffers also consume resources.

days.title: Assemble the evidence
days.action: Finish the project and curate evidence across the four territories.
days.evidence: Dossier draft and functioning demonstration.
days.retrieval: Retrieve principles independently before consulting the creed.

days.title: Rehearse under change
days.action: Run the demo with one bounded changed constraint and use your own choice of tools.
days.evidence: Rehearsal output and adaptation debrief.
days.retrieval: Explain why the chosen model fits better than an alternative.

days.title: Write the operating code
days.action: Repeat a comparable baseline scenario; prepare the next ninety days.
days.evidence: Before/after comparison, operating code and continuation plan.
days.retrieval: Identify remaining limits rather than performing certainty.

days.title: Doomsday
days.action: Demonstrate, defend one decision, respond to a bounded change and execute a next step.
days.evidence: Assessed demonstration and next action.
days.retrieval: Independent selection; no required model-name checklist.

days.title: The next ninety days
days.action: Integrate feedback, name unfinished work and schedule the first continuation review.
days.evidence: Final dossier and dated 30/60/90-day milestones.
days.retrieval: Explain what changed in behaviour and what still needs practice.

models.name: Opportunity cost
models.prompt: What is the best realistic alternative I give up?
models.limitation: Avoid valuing every free hour as if it could earn unlimited money.

models.name: Control and influence
models.prompt: What can I decide, influence or only respond to?
models.limitation: Influence is partial; do not collapse everything into total control or helplessness.

models.name: First principles
models.prompt: What is required, observed or merely assumed?
models.limitation: Do not discard accumulated expertise without a reason.

models.name: Inversion
models.prompt: What would make this fail, and what can I prevent?
models.limitation: Risk listing can become avoidance; finish with an action.

models.name: Incentives
models.prompt: What outcomes might matter to each party, and how can I check?
models.limitation: An inferred motive is not a fact.

models.name: Second-order consequences
models.limitation: Speculation is not prediction; state uncertainty.

models.name: Leverage
models.prompt: Where can a scarce resource produce more useful output?
models.limitation: Automating bad work scales bad work; include quality and maintenance costs.

models.name: Feedback loops
models.prompt: Which signal leads to which adjustment, and when?
models.limitation: Avoid optimising a vanity measure instead of the intended result.

models.name: Probabilistic thinking
models.prompt: What outcomes are plausible, and what evidence would update my confidence?
models.limitation: Numbers without a basis are false precision.

models.name: Margin of safety
models.prompt: What buffer or fallback keeps a plausible setback manageable?
models.limitation: Buffers have costs and cannot remove every risk.
